newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes fall with WTI amid thin talk.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes fall with WTI amid thin talk.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices fell moderately early Friday, tracking WTI/Cushing prices as local spot trade faded ahead of the weekend, traders said.
Following the sale of two Alaskan crude cargoes earlier this week, four to five refiners still needed to purchase barrels for March, traders said.
The two Alaskan cargoes sold at $1.30 and $1.18 a barrel under March WTI.
California posted price fell 50 cents a barrel overnight on the heals of yesterday's sharply lower NYMEX.
Wilmington's average price fell to $17.95, off 50 cents from earlier this week, while Kern River dropped about 45 cents to $16.94 a barrel.
About 1.2 million extra barrels of heavy crudes continued to pressure California markets after Tosco's damaged refinery declared force majeure on deliveries last week.
Texaco, a key heavy crude producer in Calif., was reported to own the bulk of the turned-back crude, with 30,000 of the 40,000 barrels-per-day declined by Tosco, traders said.
Confirmed prices for San Joaquin Valley heavies ranged $16.44 to 16.69 a barre.
